routing.decided_by: tiebreaks.passive_247 — two devices declare passive_247 and no study orders them

caveats: Total sleep time is the well-validated part of consumer sleep tracking, but it runs ~17 min short against PSG on average (pooled, 24 studies). Trend it; do not read it to the minute.
The other passive device reported 447 min. The tiebreak chose which to report; it did not establish which is closer to the truth.

competing.note: Not averaged. Kept so the 26 min spread stays visible.

must_disclose: A tiebreak in devices.yaml decided this, not evidence — the two devices disagree by 26 min.
Rule A is provisional: no independent head-to-head compares a 24/7 ring against a training watch for passive signals.

routing.decided_by: no_rule_applies — two devices declare passive_247 and tiebreaks.passive_247 is unset

caveats: Neither absolute value is comparable to the other or to a clinical figure: one device is documented ~15 ms low on RMSSD vs ECG, and the other has no dossier at all.
Both are usable against their own baselines separately. They are not usable against each other.

must_disclose: No rule or tiebreak resolves this. Both numbers are reported with their sources; picking one would be invention.
Set tiebreaks.passive_247 in devices.yaml to choose which device to report from — that is a preference, and will be stated as one.
